disease_label_per_paper: Vertebral osteomyelitis / masked spondylodiscitis with Campylobacter jejuni bacteremia and psoas abscess
presentation_summary: 77-year-old woman with chronic low-back pain, scoliosis, prior spinal infiltration, and daily prednisone presented with 7 days of severe diarrhea and 2 days of acute worsening of low-back pain.
Vitals including temperature were normal, but CRP and WBC were markedly elevated.
MRI showed paravertebral and left psoas inflammatory changes at L3/L4, and CT confirmed a small gas-containing abscess that was not drainable.
Blood and stool cultures grew Campylobacter jejuni; psoas fine-needle biopsy culture was negative but 16S rRNA PCR detected Campylobacter species.
